f13_resolution.pre_fix_observation: TestModuleSysPathBranch evicts and re-imports `session_buddy.cli_with_modes` via bare `sys.modules.pop()` + `importlib.import_module()`. The pollution has two layers: (1) the parent-package attribute `session_buddy.cli_with_modes` is left pointing at the freshly-imported module after the test, causing string-form `monkeypatch.setattr('session_buddy.cli_with_modes.<attr>', ...)` to resolve to the wrong module; (2) the conftest's `pytest_runtest_setup` re-attaches `utils`, `memory`, `config`, `backends`, `modes`, `cli` submodules as attributes on `session_buddy` but does NOT include `cli_with_modes` — so after the conftest re-imports `session_buddy` (e.g. when purging stubs), the `cli_with_modes` attribute is missing entirely, causing pytest's `resolve()` to fail with `AttributeError: 'module' object at session_buddy.cli_with_modes has no attribute 'cli_with_modes'`.
f13_resolution.verification: All 4 cli_with_modes::TestMain tests now pass in the full gate. The c* subset (where the issue was first reproduced) passes. The full unit test file `tests/unit/test_cli_with_modes.py` runs 61/61 with 100% coverage preserved. Memory: 'conftest-sysmodules-pollution-pattern' — both the test file (use try/finally) and the conftest (re-attach list) are part of the correct fix.
